COR-TRY-26-037, Pre-Budget 2027 and 2028 Ambulance and Equipment Procurement Approval
notes:
Kedar Tupil, Acting Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, explained that pre-budget approval is requested to support the timely acquisition and delivery of 20 replacement ambulances required for 2028.  He noted that Council approval is also requested to support the timely acquisition and delivery in 2027 of 76 defibrillators, 72 stretchers, and a replacement Electronic Patient Care Reporting System (ePCR) for Paramedic Services.

Responding to Council, Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, TITLE, explained that Council considering a pre-budget approval for paramedic equipment is a routine practice due to the lengthy process in ordering the equipment.

items.title: COR-TRY-26-038, Regional Debenture Issue Dated October 19, 2026
notes:
K. Tupil introduced the report related to the issuing of Regional Debentures. Debentures are issued to fund capital projects. The Municipal Act prescribes, among other things, that the proceeds of a debenture issue can only be used to finance capital works. Staff reviewed the progress of capital projects to determine which projects would require debenture financing in the fall of 2026. Regional capital projects from waste management, Grand River Transit, facility asset renewal, housing, Waterloo Regional Police, and paramedic services are being financed through this debenture issue along with capital projects for the cities of Cambridge, Kitchener and Waterloo and townships of Wilmot and Woolwich.

He noted that Council will be considering the debenture by-laws later in the agenda.

Received for information.

items.title: Community and Health Services Committee Summary - October 6, 2026
Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. H. Wang provided a Board of Health update. She highlighted that RSV and Flu vaccination clinics have begun around the Region in anticipation for the respiratory season. She also provided an update related to student vaccination requirements. She noted that suspension enforcement of student vaccines will begin in February for secondary schools and in April for elementary schools. She acknowledged the successful enforcement in the previous school year.

Responding to Council, Dr. H. Wang confirmed that there will be vaccination buses and the locations and dates are publicly available on the Regional website. 

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-BWR-26-008, 30 Lauris Avenue, Cambridge - Surplus Lands
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, introduced the report related to the surplus lands at 30 Lauris Avenue, Cambridge. He outlined that the awarded proposal was put forward by Central Ontario Co-operative Housing Federation (COCHF) and includes an estimated 101 dwelling units, approximately 30% (31 units) of which will be affordable for a term of not less than 63 years, with a possible extension of 36 years if both the Region and COCHF/30 Lauris Avenue Housing Co-operative Incorporated agree. COCHF submitted funding applications to Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation and to facilitate funding COCHF incorporated a housing co-operative for this project.

Council acknowledged the good work of staff both at the Regional and City level.

motions.item_title: Administration and Finance Committee Summary - October 6, 2026
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, on behalf of the Waterloo Region Education and Public Network (WREPNET) partners, renew its agreement with Rogers Communications Canada Inc. for the provisioning and supply of a dark fibre network within the Region for a five (5) year period beginning September 1, 2026, subject to final CPI reconciliation and the material terms summarized in this report, with such agreement to be satisfactory to the Commissioner of Corporate Services and Regional Solicitor, as outlined in Report COR-ITS-26-001 dated October 6, 2026. THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo directs staff to review and update the Region’s Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy for consideration by the Administration & Finance Committee in Q2 2027, as outlined in report COR-CFN-26-021 dated October 6, 2026. WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's Cultural Drivers of Tourism program provides funding from the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) Reserve to support arts, cultural, and heritage organizations that attract visitors to Waterloo Region; and WHEREAS hotels located throughout Waterloo Region generate the Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues that fund this program; and WHEREAS the 2026 funding allocations resulted in Cambridge-based organizations receiving approximately $3,000 of the $250,000 available through the program, despite Cambridge being home to a significant number of accommodation providers contributing to the MAT Reserve; WHEREAS a sustainable cultural tourism strategy should recognize both visitor attraction outcomes and the contribution of municipalities that generate the revenues supporting the program; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to review the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria to determine whether amendments are warranted to ensure a more equitable geographic distribution of funding across the Region's municipalities; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include consideration of: The relationship between Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue generation and funding allocations; Mechanisms to ensure all municipalities receive fair consideration under the program; The long-term impact of current allocation practices on cultural development and tourism growth in municipalities receiving minimal funding; and Alternative funding models that balance visitor attraction metrics with regional equity objectives. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council with recommendations prior to the next Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding intake. WHEREAS the late Kari Williams served the residents of Waterloo Region with dedication, compassion, and a strong commitment to community well-being; and WHEREAS Kari Williams was a passionate supporter of the Stanley Park Eats program, which provides meals and support to community members in need; and WHEREAS the Stanley Park Community Association is leading a community mural project on the Stanley Park Eats serving hut; and WHEREAS the mural has been inspired by Kari Williams' commitment to addressing food insecurity and supporting the Stanley Park community; and WHEREAS the project has received funding through the City of Kitchener and contributions from the Stanley Park Community Association, and community fundraising efforts; and WHEREAS community art projects help create vibrant public spaces and strengthen neighbourhood pride; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional Council approve a one-time grant of $2,000 from the Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association to support the Stanley Park Eats mural project; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Regional Council recognizes the lasting contributions of Kari Williams to the Stanley Park community and Waterloo Region; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Corporate Services be authorized to take all necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.
motions.text_html:
The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows:

  1. THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, on behalf of the Waterloo Region Education and Public Network (WREPNET) partners, renew its agreement with Rogers Communications Canada Inc. for the provisioning and supply of a dark fibre network within the Region for a five (5) year period beginning September 1, 2026, subject to final CPI reconciliation and the material terms summarized in this report, with such agreement to be satisfactory to the Commissioner of Corporate Services and Regional Solicitor, as outlined in Report COR-ITS-26-001 dated October 6, 2026.
  2. THAT the Regional Municipality of Waterloo directs staff to review and update the Region’s Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy for consideration by the Administration & Finance Committee in Q2 2027, as outlined in report COR-CFN-26-021 dated October 6, 2026.
  3. WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo's Cultural Drivers of Tourism program provides funding from the Municipal Accommodation Tax (MAT) Reserve to support arts, cultural, and heritage organizations that attract visitors to Waterloo Region; and
    WHEREAS hotels located throughout Waterloo Region generate the Municipal Accommodation Tax revenues that fund this program; and
    WHEREAS the 2026 funding allocations resulted in Cambridge-based organizations receiving approximately $3,000 of the $250,000 available through the program, despite Cambridge being home to a significant number of accommodation providers contributing to the MAT Reserve;
    WHEREAS a sustainable cultural tourism strategy should recognize both visitor attraction outcomes and the contribution of municipalities that generate the revenues supporting the program;
    THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to review the Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding formula and eligibility criteria to determine whether amendments are warranted to ensure a more equitable geographic distribution of funding across the Region's municipalities; and
    BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include consideration of:
    1. The relationship between Municipal Accommodation Tax revenue generation and funding allocations;
    2. Mechanisms to ensure all municipalities receive fair consideration under the program;
    3. The long-term impact of current allocation practices on cultural development and tourism growth in municipalities receiving minimal funding; and
    4. Alternative funding models that balance visitor attraction metrics with regional equity objectives.
      BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT staff report back to Council with recommendations prior to the next Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding intake.
  4. WHEREAS the late Kari Williams served the residents of Waterloo Region with dedication, compassion, and a strong commitment to community well-being; and
    WHEREAS Kari Williams was a passionate supporter of the Stanley Park Eats program, which provides meals and support to community members in need; and
    WHEREAS the Stanley Park Community Association is leading a community mural project on the Stanley Park Eats serving hut; and
    WHEREAS the mural has been inspired by Kari Williams' commitment to addressing food insecurity and supporting the Stanley Park community; and
    WHEREAS the project has received funding through the City of Kitchener and contributions from the Stanley Park Community Association, and community fundraising efforts; and
    WHEREAS community art projects help create vibrant public spaces and strengthen neighbourhood pride;
    THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Regional Council approve a one-time grant of $2,000 from the Public Art Reserve Fund to the Stanley Park Community Association to support the Stanley Park Eats mural project; and
    BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that Regional Council recognizes the lasting contributions of Kari Williams to the Stanley Park community and Waterloo Region; and
    BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Corporate Services be authorized to take all necessary administrative actions to implement this resolution.
